Photograph: ZUMA Press, Inc./Alamy Reform UK Cambridge University examines conduct of academic suspended by Reform UK James Orr, an associate professor, was shown in Channel 4 News footage apparently trying to sidestep electoral law Anna Isaac and Rowena Mason Fri 4 Sep 2026 13.48 EDT Last modified on Fri 4 Sep 2026 14.14 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Cambridge University has said it is examining the conduct of James Orr, its associate professor and a top Reform UK aide, after he was filmed appearing to try to circumvent electoral laws on foreign political donations. Orr, the suspended head of policy for Reform, is one of two senior officials to step aside after claims that he orchestrated a plot to have polling paid for by a foreign firm – something that is impermissible under British electoral law. The academic was filmed by a group of investigative journalists called Verbatim, founded by the Centre for Climate Reporting, seemingly attempting to sidestep election laws. In a statement shared with the Guardian, a spokesperson for the University of Cambridge said: “The university is looking into these matters.” Orr is an associate professor of religion at Cambridge’s divinity faculty and teaches students at the university. 1:15 Footage from the Channel 4 News and Verbatim undercover investigation into Reform finances – video Little known outside UK and US political circles, Orr has been a highly influential intellectual force within Reform. He was labelled the party’s “philosopher king” by the news organisation Politico. A key attraction for senior figures in Reform when appointing Orr was his high-level US political contacts within the Maga movement. JD Vance, the US vice-president, has called him his “intellectual mentor” and his “British Sherpa”. Footage broadcast by Channel 4 News on Thursday night showed an undercover reporter posing as a UK-based supporter in conversation with Orr. Orr discussed commissioning polling that was secretly organised by Reform, but suggested it be paid for by a US company belonging to the fake supporter’s supposed father. Farage seeks to shore up damaged leadership as scandal engulfs Reform conference Read more In a separate clip, Orr can be heard saying of the poll funding arrangement that Nigel Farage “doesn’t know, won’t know” and it is the kind of thing he would “rather not know”. Reform UK initially described the Channel 4 News and Verbatim investigation as a “hoax”. On Thursday evening, Orr posted a video on his X account in which he said: “There is absolutely no way this could amount to a benefit or donation in kind at all.” He dismissed Verbatim as “politically motivated actors trying to discredit a political opponent through dubious legal means”. Still, on Friday morning he and Dan Jukes, a senior aide to Farage who has also denied wrongdoing, stood down pending an internal party investigation into the claims raised by the broadcast. Farage, who was also featured in the investigation meeting with the fake supporters, distanced himself from Orr and Jukes on Friday. The party leader told reporters: “The two individuals involved are not even part of our fundraising team, so they should have gone through the appropriate channels. Checks would have been made and they would never, ever have got to sit down at a table with me.” The Guardian has approached Orr for comment. Directors Postpone Decision on Eurovision 2027 Participation by Louie Pilbrow 16 September 2026 2 minute read Melody rehearsing ESA DIVA for Spain at St. Jakobshalle Spanish media reports that the Board of Directors of the Spanish public broadcaster RTVE, after meeting this week, have postponed making a decision on participation in the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest. RAC 1 reports that the Board of Directors of RTVE, having met on Wednesday morning, have postponed the debate on Spanish participation in the Eurovision Song Contest 2027 to a later date, which is currently unknown. The broadcaster is also reported to have requested an extension to make their decision from the European Broadcasting Union (EBU). This has similarly been granted by the EBU to Belgian broadcaster VRT, Dutch broadcasting corporation NPO and new Hungarian broadcaster MRTV. The RTVE Board had discussed whether to return to the competition having boycotted the 2026 contest due to the continued participation of Israel in the contest, or to continue to boycott the competition. The Spanish broadcaster was one of five broadcasters across Europe that withdrew from competing in the Eurovision Song Contest 2026, following Israel’s inclusion in this year’s contest. In December 2025, RTVE outlined in detail its reasons for not competing in the 70th edition of the competition. Of the five broadcasters that opted to boycott Eurovision 2026, AVROTROS (Netherlands) is the first broadcaster to confirm its continued non-participation in Eurovision 2027. RÚV (Iceland), RTÉ (Ireland), RTVSLO (Slovenia) and RTVE (Spain) have yet to officially state their positions. Source: RAC 1 Spain in the Eurovision Song Contest + Spain debuted in the Eurovision Song Contest in 1961 and competed annually until 2026. Spain has won the contest on two occasions. The first time was in 1968, when Massiel sang “La la la”. and the second time was in 1969, when Salomé sang “Vivo cantando”. 1969 is the only year where more than one song has won the contest. The 1969 contest saw a four-way tie between Spain, France, the United Kingdom and the Netherlands.
